Committee Minutes of the People's Majlis

22nd Meeting of the Independent Institutions Committee

13 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis Lh Building (Committee Room 5)

Start time: 11:00

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for Maafushi constituency, Hussain Riza Adam}

Remarks by the Chair:

Assalaamu alaikum. Yes! I welcome all members attending the 22nd meeting of the Independent Institutions Committee of the People's Majlis. Attending this meeting are the Honourable Member for West Henveyru constituency, Ali Ibrahim; the Honourable Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef; the Honourable Member for Kolamaafushi constituency, Ibrahim Didi; the Honourable Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed; the Honourable Member for Dhidhdhoo constituency, Abdul Latheef Mohamed; and the Honourable Member for South Fuvahmulah constituency, Ibrahim Hussain. On today's agenda is reviewing the 2025 annual report of the Civil Service Commission and, based on it, sharing the presentation submitted by the Commission together with the members of the Commission. Then, after that presentation is made, members will have the opportunity to ask those officials further questions if they wish to clarify anything. So, at this point I will call on the members of the Civil Service Commission. (After a short while) Assalaamu alaikum. We called the members of the Civil Service Commission because we have received the 2025 report that you prepared and sent us. Now a summary presentation on it will proceed. Then after that, if members have any questions they wish to ask, or anything they wish to clarify, I will give that opportunity. Attending this meeting from the Civil Service are the President of the Commission, Al-Ustaz Mohamed Mujthaz; the Vice President of the Commission, Al-Faazila Mohamed Nishu; Member of the Commission, Al-Faazila Fathimath Habeeba; Member of the Commission, Dr. Hussain Faiz; Member of the Commission, Dr. Deeba Moosa; and the Counsel General, Al-Ustaz Ibrahim Rasheed. I welcome all of you, okay. Then, after the presentation, could each of you please state your name when you speak! That is to make it easier when writing the minutes. So, Ustaz, please go ahead!

Remarks by the Counsel General of the Civil Service Commission, Ibrahim Rasheed:

Yes! Thank you. I am Ibrahim Rasheed, Counsel General. First of all, I thank the Honourable Members for giving us this opportunity. Today I am presenting the highlights of the Civil Service Commission's 2025 annual report for your information. In that regard, first, looking at the important matters we wish to note regarding the administrative arrangements relating to civil service employees, amendments were made to the Civil Service Regulation in 2025. Accordingly, we made 3 main amendments to the Civil Service Regulation. Overall, these include the amendment made to arrange leave for employees for special health needs; the amendment we made to the regulation regarding the pension and gratuity money of retired employees when they are re-appointed to a state post; and in addition, the amendment made to the regulation regarding the dress code for civil service employees; making a total of 3 amendments to the regulation. In addition, some amendments were also made in 2025 to other regulations within the civil service sector. Accordingly, the 2nd amendment to the Immigration Officers Regulation was made, while the regulation on working hours, leave and holidays of Aviation Security Command officers, and the regulation on how senior executive staff act, were abolished during 2025, okay. And looking at the matters to note regarding changes made to the policies we follow and the introduction of new policies, the policy "Allowances given to civil service employees" was amended. In addition, a policy on selecting and appointing persons to the post of Secretary General of local councils was compiled, and implementation in line with that policy has begun. Along with that, a policy was established for transferring employees below the public service ranks of the State Pay Framework to the public service ranks upon obtaining a degree, and implementation of it has begun. Some amendments were also made to these same policies during that year. Accordingly, an amendment was made to the policy on selecting and appointing persons to nurses' job matrix posts. Along with that, the policy on transferring those in ranks below the public service ranks of the State Pay Framework job matrix to the public service ranks upon obtaining a degree

was also amended during that year. Overall, looking at this floor, where major changes have come to the Civil Service Regulation, our first regulation was compiled in 2008. It was later revised and a regulation compiled in 2010, and the one now in force is the Civil Service Regulation 2014, okay. Although the Maldives Civil Service Regulation 2014 has been in force, nineteen amendments have so far been made to the regulation, along with important changes that needed to be made to it at the time. And we are now carrying out the work of compiling Civil Service 2026. Looking at the statistics on approving the structures of civil service offices, seventy-two structures were approved in civil service offices during 2025. Of these, sixteen structures of ministries, five structures of city councils, ten structures of atoll councils and fifty structures of island councils, in addition to six hospital structures and ten structures for other civil service offices, were approved. Along with that, among employees' job structures, thirty-six structures were compiled during 2025, four structures were approved, and six structures were amended during that year. Looking at the statistics on the number of employees appointed to jobs in 2025, and on employees' job transfers and dismissals, four thousand three hundred and seventy employees were newly appointed to jobs during 2025. And four hundred and fifteen employees' jobs were transferred. Looking at the statistics on promotions given, promotions were given to nineteen hundred and thirty-five employees. And the number of employees who left or were dismissed from their jobs for various reasons is fifteen hundred and seven employees. In this regard, looking at the time generally taken in the job appointment stage, in 2025 we attended to a large number of job requests within three days. Accordingly, the number of these requests that we attended to within three days is five thousand two hundred and sixty-one. And while two thousand three hundred and eighty requests were attended to between four days and seven days, two hundred and twenty-seven requests were attended to between eight days and fifteen days. And more than sixteen days

were taken for one hundred and ninety-three requests. Generally, looking at the time spent between advertising and filling a job, jobs were filled for one hundred and forty-six requests within thirty days. And jobs were filled for thirteen hundred and twenty-eight requests between thirty days and sixty days. Jobs were filled for four hundred and forty-one requests between sixty days and seventy days. Jobs were filled for three hundred and fifty requests between seventy days and eighty days, for two hundred and forty-one requests between eighty days and ninety days, and for nine hundred and fourteen requests that exceeded ninety days. Looking at the extent to which offices act in line with the regulation in sending job-related requests, while we received a total of eight thousand and sixty-one requests during 2025, of these, approximately half were processed after being submitted once, submitted once by the office. That is four thousand and thirty-nine requests. Those are requests processed with the first submission. However, some requests were processed even after being submitted two or three times. Accordingly, three thousand one hundred and fifteen requests were processed after being submitted twice. And seven hundred and ninety-six requests after being submitted four times, and the number of requests processed after being submitted more than four times also reaches one hundred and eleven. Then, overall, looking at the statistics on complaints submitted to the Commission relating to jobs, especially relating to the job appointment stage, five thousand seven hundred and two complaints relating to job appointments were submitted to us during 2025. During that year, five thousand six hundred and thirty-one complaints were concluded and the submitting parties were responded to. At the end of 2025, we had not concluded responses to seventy-one complaints. Then, overall, an average period of five days was taken to respond to complaints submitted in this way. Then, looking at the work done to ensure that offices follow the regulations and policies relating to appointing employees, for one thing, an employment audit matrix was created, and employment audits, auditing of employment requests, have begun in a special way. And in addition, this

cases of dismissal from jobs contrary to the regulation have been arranged to proceed directly on the advice of the Legal Section. And along with that, an Employee Relations Section was created to attend to job-related complaints, and requests submitted relating to jobs have been attended to under that section's oversight. And an e-recruitment system was introduced, and the work of filling jobs through e-recruitment has now begun for some sectors. Then, looking at the statistics on cases submitted to courts relating to appointments to and dismissals from jobs, a total of fourteen cases relating to job appointments were submitted to court in 2025. Of these, while seven cases were concluded during that year, six of those cases were won in favour of the Civil Service Commission. So, in these six cases it was determined that the Civil Service Commission acted in line with the law and regulations in the job appointment process. So, the percentage of cases submitted to courts that the Commission won is 86%. Only one case was concluded against the Commission during that year. Accountability to the government and the Majlis: looking at this area, regarding the extent to which employees support implementing government policies, and the extent to which permanent secretaries and responsible officials carry out their responsibilities, we began this year to look at the quality of the work of permanent secretaries and responsible officials. First, the policies that permanent secretaries and responsible officials must follow were developed and strengthened, and implementation in line with those policies has begun. And along with that, complaints submitted concerning permanent secretaries and responsible senior officials are looked into, and if the Commission finds there is a situation requiring action against those parties, the work of taking that action has also proceeded as part of holding them accountable, okay. Then, looking at the statistics on Commission meetings, unlike 2024, the number of Commission meetings in 2025 increased greatly. Accordingly, eighty-seven formal Commission meetings were held in 2025. And while three meetings of the Commission's Advisory Committee were held, three hundred and fifty of the meetings held as the Commission's daily briefings were held in 2025. Then, of permanent secretaries and responsible senior officials'

evaluating their work performance and giving those officials marks was also something we did during 2025, giving it very high priority. Especially as part of the work of holding those officials accountable. In this regard, what I am showing here is the overall average level of those officials' marks, okay. Those who got the highest marks are between 95% and 98%. Those who got the lowest marks are between 62% and 76%. Then, the further work that needs to be done regarding these marks is still being carried out by the Commission. This is an additional graphic view of the statistics just shown. Looking at complaints submitted to the Commission, the statistics on complaints submitted to the various areas of the Commission in 2025: accordingly, while two hundred and four complaints were submitted to the Legal Affairs Division, one hundred and seventy-nine of them were concluded. It is noted that twenty-five complaints were ongoing at the end of that year. While twenty-six complaints were submitted relating to performance management, all twenty-six of those complaints were answered during that year. And while five thousand seven hundred and two complaints were submitted relating to recruitment work, five thousand six hundred and thirty-one complaints were answered during that year. And at the end of that year, we had not answered seventy-one complaints. Then, overall, five thousand nine hundred and thirty complaints relating to various areas were submitted to the Civil Service Commission during this year. Of these, the Civil Service Commission looked into the matters and responded to the submitting parties regarding five thousand eight hundred and thirty-four complaints. Then, looking at the overall time spent resolving complaints, complaints relating to administrative structure and promotion were generally resolved within four days. And complaints submitted relating to performance appraisal were resolved within a period between three days and five days. In addition, complaints of the kind that must be answered by obtaining information through the office, or by sending them to the concerned ministry, were concluded on average within sixty days. Then in addition, complaints of the kind that must be decided along with a Commission decision or a Commission opinion were generally concluded within a period between seven days and ten days. Looking at the area of accountability, regarding the statistics on cases submitted for violating the Civil Service Code of Conduct

in 2025, the number of cases submitted through the CS network and resolved is sixty-four. And an average period of sixty days was spent resolving the cases. That means that in this way too, 96.46% of the cases submitted in 2025 were concluded during that year and the parties responded to. Very robust, transparent policies for taking action against employees have been established in the civil service. And the policies have been set out in a way that ensures procedural fairness and substantive fairness, especially in taking action against employees. Accordingly, Chapter 28 of the Civil Service Regulation states that in taking action against any employee, an investigation report must be prepared, and after giving the employee the opportunity to respond based on that report, action must be taken against the employee at a level proportionate to the offence the employee commits. So, to ensure these things, the Commission did a great deal of work during this year and the policies were implemented. Looking at the area of human resource development and training, a great deal of work was done during 2025. And in addition, looking at the overall policies followed in providing education and training as part of training human resources, a policy for training civil service employees was compiled starting from 1 January 2016 and is being implemented. We are still implementing those policies. And in addition, a programme for inducting civil service employees into their jobs has been carried out every single year since 2012 for those newly appointed to jobs. In addition, every year a civil service training directory is compiled, and the work of training employees of civil service offices proceeds in line with that directory. Looking at the statistics on the training conducted in this way, compared with 2024, the number of trainings in 2025 also increased greatly. Accordingly, a total of eighteen thousand four hundred and nine employees were trained in 2025. The number of trainings held in this way is three hundred and eighty-six. And trainings were also conducted online for employees, including many who work in the atolls. In this regard, the number of employees who took part in online trainings

is nine thousand eight hundred and twenty-two. And in addition, the Commission has conducted trainings for very many parties when a specific training was needed in connection with special requests made to the Commission. Accordingly, training was also conducted for three thousand four hundred and seventy-four parties in connection with requests the Commission received. Then, civil service employees were also trained with foreign assistance; to the extent we got the opportunity to do so, we keep providing trainings. And giving it very high priority, the Commission has carried out the dealings needed with foreign parties to train employees abroad and keeps obtaining training opportunities. Accordingly, in 2025, training was given to one hundred and ten persons from India, twenty-five parties from China, and one person from Japan, one person from Singapore, and one person from Thailand, and two persons from Turkey, and one person with the assistance of the UN. Looking at the area of research and innovation, in 2025 we gave very great importance, among the government's policies, to bringing civil service standards into a digital system and making every area of the civil service an area where services can be provided digitally. Accordingly, among the work we did, in 2025 we introduced a compliance module. That is to establish a mechanism through which the various complaints and various concerns that employees submit to the Civil Service Commission can be submitted and answered through an online system. So, that system was established and implementation began in 2025. And in addition, the work of enhancing the civil service network, and the work of the contingent module, which is to update information relating to temporary employees. And the work of enhancing My Account was also done by us in 2025. In addition, looking at our ongoing projects, the work on a training module is now nearly complete and we have begun the testing stage. This is to carry out the training of employees through an online system. And the work on the exam module is now being prepared, through the ITC itself. This is a module being prepared so that the exams that must be conducted in recruiting employees to various civil service offices proceed in a transparent manner through an online and digital platform. Along with that, our

violation module work is now complete and the testing stage has begun, okay. The violation module is a module being prepared to build a system through which action against civil service employees can be taken transparently through a digital system, to ensure that action is taken with fairness and justice and in line with the established procedures. As I said earlier, the work on this module is also now complete and the testing stage is proceeding. Along with that, we are working to add some more sectors to the online recruitment module. In particular, our goal is to arrange for the recruitment of as many sectors as possible to proceed online by the end of this year. Then, looking at the area of monitoring and reporting, overall, looking at the statistics on audits carried out in 2025, four audits were carried out as special audits. These include the audit of Dh. Kudahuvadhoo and NSPA, and the audit of Malé City Council and L. Gan Regional Hospital. And five audits were carried out as spot audits. That is, regarding granting leave for special health needs, and because issues with hospital overtime were noted, and to determine the extent to which service charters have been compiled in offices, and regarding some issues submitted relating to the LRA. And in addition, to determine the extent to which offices have complied regarding updating the contingent module. In this regard, HR, and in addition, one audit was carried out as an HR audit in 2025. That is an HR audit of the Centre for People with Special Needs. Then, we carried out the work of monitoring internal compliance audits in 2025. Accordingly, as part of offices establishing an internal compliance audit system, it is determined that each office must audit and send a report every year. To carry out an internal audit and compliance audit of that office and send the report to the Commission. Accordingly, after the Commission spot-checks among them, the Commission is now carrying out the work of reviewing the reports it selects and informing those offices of the matters in them that need to be corrected. Looking at the challenges in the work of the civil service and the work done to resolve them, one of the biggest challenges the Commission faces, as noted, is that the Commission

has not received an adequate budget. However, in 2026 we received an additional budget component in connection with the People's Majlis and the President's Office. Then, along with that, the low number of staff working at the Commission's office is a very big challenge we face. While the Civil Service Commission is an office overseeing the affairs of approximately six hundred and ninety offices and overseeing the affairs of around thirty-five thousand employees, we have to work with very few staff. Then, as a result of the work done in this way, we received six additional staff in 2026. However, given how our work stands, it is still noted that the number of staff is low. Then, in addition, while the Civil Service Commission has the responsibility for running these training programmes, the responsibility for running training for every sector of the Maldives, we have received a very small budget for this too. Then, as part of this work, funds for training have now also been increased in our 2026 budget. Then, the shortage of space in the Commission's office building is a very big difficulty we now face, okay. We now face very great difficulties in managing staff affairs because of the lack of space in the building. Then, regarding this matter too, we are talking with the relevant parties of the government. On a way for us to expand the office base or to get a good space at another location. Along with that, the work of compiling the civil service strategic action, strategic plan for 2026 to 2030 was carried out during 2025. Accordingly, this plan has been compiled and implementation has now also begun, okay. Then, the work of designing CS Network 3.0 is the work we wanted to give top priority to during this past year. And it is one of the works we want to give top priority to this year too, that is, to move to a fully digital system under the government's digital policy. However, because we have not obtained developers for this project either, the work is currently stalled. The work of finding developers for us is still proceeding. Then in addition, a human resource audit of the Commission was carried out and we have now received the results of that audit. That is regarding the Commission's various

areas, how the structure should be, and the number of staff required. Then, based on the audit results, the Commission is now carrying out the work of implementing those matters and making the changes needed to the structure. Along with that, during 2025 we did the work of establishing a call centre. As a result, a call centre has now been established; one of the biggest complaints of the general public and of civil servants seeking services regarding the civil service has been the difficulties in the Civil Service Commission answering the phone. To resolve that, the work of establishing a call centre was done and a call centre established, and that issue has now been resolved. Then, along with that, obtaining opportunities to train civil service employees abroad is something we have planned going forward. Then, regarding this, I would note that work is currently under way in collaboration with India, China, Singapore, Pakistan, Turkey, Malaysia, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. This is, overall, a summary of the matters highlighted in our 2025 annual report, okay. Thank you.

Remarks by the Chair:

Yes! Thank you very much, okay. The Honourable Member for South Galolhu constituency, Meekail Ahmed Nasym, has now joined our meeting. Generally, the committee also receives some complaints relating to the civil service. Our committee has received about four complaints, and of these, the information on two complaints has now been clarified, from private parties, and the work of responding to those parties from this side will proceed before the end of this month. Sometimes members' complaints come regarding attendance. However, no such complaint has come this time yet. So, I take it that all members are attending regularly. God willing, we will very soon hold a visit to the Commission, a visit by members. That is because the budget will be passed before the end of this session. So, there are four or five challenges just highlighted. So, we too will go and visit that place and look at it further; in my view,

it is very important. So, in my view, when the budget is discussed then, we in the Independent Institutions Committee will also have the opportunity to give that advice and counsel to the Finance Committee. I will open the floor to members. If you wish to say anything about the presentation made, or about any other matter related to the Civil Service Commission. I give the floor to the Honourable Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef.

Remarks by the Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef:

Yes! Thank you, Chair. Welcome, members of the Civil Service Commission. I want to clarify two things relating to the report just presented, and in addition one thing relating to a complaint received from the public. It was just said that there are few administrative staff to manage the affairs of about thirty-five thousand employees now. And the report only says that they are few. And on all the other matters there are recommendations given, such and such a thing like this. For example, under the things achieved, such and such a thing was done, this was achieved. For example, the call centre work was considered important, it was started, and it is now being implemented, that is how that stands. But on this matter, nothing specific is said like that; since it is not said that a specific number, this many administrative staff, is needed to manage the affairs of these thirty-five thousand employees, I want to clarify a little how many you need. Then, the second thing I want to clarify is the issue of councils' SGs, about which very many complaints are being received, okay. On the SGs' issue, that complaint comes from every direction. So, how are you now thinking about that matter? Then, the other matter is one on which this committee has also received a complaint. That is regarding employees' certificates: when certain kinds of certificates are obtained, an allowance is given as an allowance for that certificate, okay. And that employee has also worked very hard to do that. Then the Civil Service Commission says it is something that must be given. Something that must be received. But this young person works at the Police Service Commission, in the police. And that side says that it cannot be given because a regulation has not been made, or because a policy for giving it has not been made. For this long, can that

be kept up like that? For example, when a young person acquires a certain kind of knowledge and gets a certificate, in receiving what must be received, is it the Civil Service Commission that will manage this? Is that a civil service employee? So, can it be kept like that for so long without making that policy? How is it? Those are the three things I want to clarify.

Remarks by the Chair:

Yes! It would be good to state your name and proceed.

Remarks by the President of the Civil Service Commission, Mohamed Mujthaz:

Yes! Thank you very much. I am the President of the Civil Service Commission, Mohamed Mujthaz. First of all, when the Chair of the Committee, Al-Ustaz Hussain Riza Adam, spoke of visiting the Commission, of committee members visiting, we very much welcome that. And we are very happy. When you come, the Honourable Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef, will also get the answer to the question he asked. And I believe you will get a very good opportunity to see with your own eyes the environment in which our staff are working. We will show you every corner and do all of this. That is, you will then accept that the place where staff work is not yet an environment suitable for staff to work in. Put another way, because of the shortage in our building and all sorts of things, we have to be in a way that people doing important work should not have to be. Moreover, in this day and age, we also have a training institute, people come from various places. And there are also people in difficult health conditions. They have to go up and down by the stairs. A lift, this is the age of lifts. A place without a lift, a very old place, this Civil Service Commission. Then, having noted these matters, the first question asked by the Honourable Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef, the number of office staff. Looking at the number, it is noted

that we now have approximately, this past year there would have been approximately eighty or so staff, I think, okay, excluding members. About eighty staff. Now it will approach one hundred, or may reach one hundred. It will just about reach one hundred this year, okay. However, you will see the work of the PA. That is a very big job, the work relating to secretaries general and permanent secretaries. Those doing that work, last year there were three staff including the supervisor. So, that too is a very difficult thing. Then, the area where our greatest concern lies now is IT, okay. For IT we are struggling because we simply cannot get suitable good staff. Now in IT, working as consultants, excluding consultants, there are three staff. That is two staff along with one supervisor. And those other two staff too were brought in, two young people who are still studying, because we could not get people. Uh, then something gets done, doesn't it, when we use those young people too to do these things. Considering the salary and all these matters, it is very difficult for us to get IT people. That is a very big challenge for us. Very many of our matters, the work of the whole Commission, is mainly built on IT. So, to the extent this part is weak, it also affects our work in other areas. Then, in answering the question asked as the second question, I want to ask a question, I want to clarify something with the Honourable Member. What are the complaints about SGs regarding? (After a short while) Yes! Thank you very much. I think perhaps you met with us on a very good day. There are quite a lot of challenges for us in appointing SGs. They were not appointed before. Finally, we appointed SGs during 2025. The reason is that some elections also came up, and again, with the new councils coming at the start of 2026 and all these matters, we also had to wait. Then, along with some of our, very many concerns, along with concerns about these kinds of matters, I was also looking at how a solution to this could be obtained, including from the Attorney General's Office, and carrying out these matters. Then again, when we looked into appointing, the SGs' salary suddenly increased. It increased on 1 November

2025. It increased by a very large amount. Having increased, again a lot of pressure kept coming to us from councils, from people wanting to come to that post. Then the news suddenly heard was that the SGs' salary had decreased by a very large amount. When that happened, there was also great dissatisfaction from SGs towards us. In reality, it is not a matter that concerns us in any way, the salary matters; the decrease in SGs' salary has no connection with us. The only connection with us is that we have to inform them of that decision of the Pay Commission. That is our role. Then, there are concerns like these. Then, what I want to tell you today is, today is 13 October 2026. Today we will advertise the secretary general posts whose terms are close to expiring, the current secretaries general, and the secretaries general whose terms are close to expiring in December. For the answer to the third question, I think I would request that a member from among the members, or the CG, answer this.

Remarks by the Counsel General of the Civil Service Commission, Ibrahim Rasheed:

Yes! Thank you, Honourable Member. On the question asked regarding the certificate allowance: now that employees have moved to the State Pay Framework, all civil service employees having moved over on 1 November 2025, although an allowance was given as a certificate allowance in some sectors previously, now overall, in the State Pay Framework, there is no arrangement for giving a certificate allowance upon obtaining a specific certificate, okay. However, there are still such policies to some extent in some sectors. In that regard, what we note is that in the education sector, especially for teachers, when teachers obtain a master's certificate, together with four years of experience, there is still provision within the Pay Commission's standards for those employees to progress to a further post. In other sectors, overall, since the Pay Framework came, no policies or standards have been set for progressing upon obtaining a specific certificate. Then, as I think we noted in the presentation too, with the Commission taking the lead, the Commission's vision is that Maldivian

civil service should be made up of people who have studied to first-degree level, and to that end, after consulting with the Pay Commission too, we compiled a special policy on the Commission's initiative. As I also noted just now, it is a policy compiled to move employees below public service rank seven, among the standards of the State Pay Framework, to public service rank seven if they have obtained a degree, okay. Then, from the point we compiled that policy and began implementing it, offices have been acting in line with that policy. Then, a challenge that may arise here at times is that, even within the policy, we are able to give advancement in that post, or change the post, when an office writes to the Finance Ministry and the Finance Ministry arranges that budget. In such a case an office may face a challenge. If an office facing that situation deals with us, we will work to resolve that matter. Otherwise, we have not noted a situation where this certificate promotion, or something upon obtaining a certificate, has not been given because a specific policy has not been established. Then, one situation that arose was in the education sector, as I said, when promotion after four years, promotion to a post, was looked into, there was a small issue in the Pay Framework standard at that time. At that time, the salary of rank three was lower than the salary of the third grade of rank two. If that is the case, moving anyone to the other rank would produce no result, would it? Then we had to talk with the Pay Commission to resolve that issue. So, after talking with the Pay Commission, with the Pay Commission resolving the rank three salary, we have informed offices to proceed with the work of migrating employees who meet the requirements for rank three in the education sector too. Thank you.

Remarks by the Member for Kelaa constituency, Abdulla Shareef:

I want to clarify one more small thing. I want to look into it because I do some work in the Finance Committee, and since it is a related matter. It would be very good if you could give me your opinion on this. Now, between SGs and council presidents of councils,

on these matters of the salary difference between them, what is your opinion, the Commission's alone, on what the best way to practise it actually is?

Remarks by the President of the Civil Service Commission, Mohamed Mujthaz:

I think an answer given sitting here could turn out very badly, couldn't it? This is something I too would have to do after carrying out some studies and looking into things. Now, the first problem that arose was that on 1 November 2025 the SGs' salary increased by a very large amount, it became higher than the council president's. The council president, twenty-five thousand. Thirty-five thousand for SGs. So, the council presidents' concerns are very great. In reality, as I believe, the council president is the highest party in running the whole place; the secretary general must report to the council president. The secretary general is the highest administrative party there to implement these decisions the council makes. So, I do not believe that SGs' salary should be higher than the council president's. However, that is how the matter turned out. Mainly, the Pay Commission said at the time that what falls to them is only the secretaries general. That it is this Majlis that determines the salaries of councillors and members of commissions in these matters. So, then the Pay Commission carried out the Pay Commission's responsibility. When it was carried out, some dissatisfaction also came, and very recently, starting from August, starting from August this year, the salary was again reduced. Then, as I said before, our job became informing them of that. So, perhaps we too can give the best answer on this only after carrying out some studies.

Remarks by the Chair:

Yes, I give the floor to the Honourable Member for South Fuvahmulah constituency, Ibrahim Hussain.

Remarks by the Member for South Fuvahmulah constituency, Ibrahim Hussain:

Yes! Thank you, Honourable Chair. I am very pleased with the complete report the Civil Service Commission came to the Majlis and presented. And from the report we have seen, it must be noted that, comparing 2025 with 2026, you have greatly improved your work, okay. Then however, what we have just heard is that, in reality, the relationship that should exist between the Pay Commission and the Civil Service Commission does not exist; that is what became evident to us from what you said. That is, when salaries are set, when salaries are set for civil service employees, the guardian of civil service employees in particular is the Civil Service Commission. The party that must take the most responsibility in that matter is the Civil Service Commission. That being so, if the Civil Service Commission and the Pay Commission had talked properly, studied this properly and done these things, I do not think this salary problem would have arisen in the way you just described. I believe it is because it was not done that way that the matter went the way it did. In particular, as you just said, when the SG's salary became higher than the council president's, that is not something anyone would accept. In reality, it is done according to the hierarchy, according to job matters. And no matter who did it. I cannot accept that it should happen that way. I have just two or three questions. The first question is: in a civil servant's case, if any case has been submitted, has anything happened or taken place at the Civil Service Commission whereby, through the influence of any political figure, a civil servant would not get their due? That is the first question. The second question is: we are talking about employees, or civil servants, working to obtain career advancement. For anyone to obtain their due, education, education is something that is needed. Skills are developed by doing a great deal of work to develop that person's skills, by obtaining a great deal of education, by gaining a great deal of experience, by spending a great deal of time. But after doing so, from what you say, we learn that they are now not getting the benefit or salary advancement they should get, okay. So, will you give thought to this? Then the third question is: on an island, on an island other than Malé, for those who obtain a master's, the salary advancement comes three years later

reportedly. But what has happened before in Malé, I have this case that has come to me, in particular three or four teachers from a school in Fuvahmulah have raised that issue. That issue comes to me in particular. At that time, when it happened that way, because they did not get advancement, they met me very many times, and on my trips to Fuvahmulah too, they have come across me very many times and talked. But if someone obtains that degree or master's from a school in Malé, or from a college in Malé, or from a university, that person gets those benefits immediately. However, when someone in Fuvahmulah obtains this master's from a college in Fuvahmulah, that salary advancement is not received and it drags on for many days. Will you give thought to this? What things are you doing to find a solution to this? Thank you very much for the opportunity given.

Remarks by the President of the Civil Service Commission, Mohamed Mujthaz:

Thank you very much. I will answer the first question. Then I request that others among us answer the remaining questions. Does any kind of influence come to us from political figures, or from Majlis members? What I want to ask you is: is it right for Majlis members to call members of the Civil Service Commission about such and such a matter? Is it the best thing to say, on such and such a matter, hire such and such a person? Even if that is said, we work with fairness and equality, within the regulation, as best we can, to secure the rights of all employees. Our regulation, the Civil Service Regulation, is a regulation that very strongly ensures these things. And even if any party says to do such and such a thing for such and such a person, it is not something we are able to do. Even if we wanted to do it, it is not something that can be done under the regulation. Now, for example, I will mention one thing. Leave given for special health needs. This leave is arranged after looking at very many matters. It is not leave given for every single thing. Now, for example, we have given it to someone, and without any influence, looking at what comes before us, if we

determined that this person is someone it cannot be given to, then another person comes from a somewhat powerful position. They come and say that this must be arranged for this person, the member for that island's constituency, or another connected party. We cannot do it for them. Nor will we do it. The way it would be is doing it for one person; I do not accept doing it for the person who comes that way, while not doing it for one of two people in the same situation. Then I, it does come, albeit rarely, okay. Then it will come, won't it. Out of helping someone connected to various people, to officials, out of doing things for one another, those talks will come even as far as us. By human nature, if a matter concerns a party connected to us, we too could pass it on to other parties. In that way, it does come, albeit rarely. Even if it comes, what we say is that for these kinds of reasons we will do that matter just the way it is, okay. Thank you very much.

Remarks by the Counsel General of the Civil Service Commission, Ibrahim Rasheed:

Yes! Thank you, Honourable Member. The question noted, then the question noted is, I think, the concern about salary advancement not being received upon studying or upon obtaining further education. We would not say that there are, in any way, specific policies under which salary advancement is not received upon obtaining education. However, what is currently set within the Pay Framework standards is that progression is from a rank for which the education and experience for that rank have been obtained. Then, even now there are standards within the Pay Framework under which employees get advancement, okay. Every employee, after serving two years in their rank, if that employee gets marks above 85% in their performance appraisal, then after two years every employee will move to the next step, okay. That is the policy. Then, along with that, if there is a further job in the office relating to the field in which that employee obtains education, there is no obstacle to advertising it through the existing policies, advertising that job and recruiting to that job, okay. So, within those policies, there is already an opportunity for those who obtain education, okay. Then what was noted is that, having obtained a master's in the atolls, a period is taken.

[stamp]

However, that if obtained in Malé, there are standards under which a job is appointed immediately. Then, there is nothing set in any of our policies, and so far nothing set in that way in any policy set by the Pay Commission either, okay. Then, something that may arise at times is, for example, regarding the certificate obtained, sometimes something needs further clarification or further verification, and when it has not been verified, those delays may at times arise administratively. But there are no differences in a promotion that is due upon obtaining a master's, or upon obtaining some other certificate, when obtained from a particular place. Then, as I said before, when employees migrated to the new Pay Framework, changes came in that standard to the policy for progressing upon obtaining a master's, especially in the education sector. Previously, before migrating to the Pay Framework, upon obtaining a master's that employee would move to the post directly. However, from the point of moving to the Pay Framework standard, four years of experience after obtaining the master's is a requirement for that rank. So, it is set so that it can be given if the employee has a master's and four years of experience. Then of course, a situation where such a complaint might reasonably come from an employee is that, at the stage of moving to the Pay Framework, all those who had a master's were taken to master's level. However, if a master's is obtained after moving to the Pay Framework, that person will of course move after four years, in line with the rank requirement. So, that kind of standard is what is now set. As was noted then, no difference at all is set in the standards regarding a certificate obtained in this way from a particular island or within the atolls, okay.

Remarks by the Chair:

So, we will conclude the meeting at this point. I sincerely thank all members of the Civil Service Commission for coming, and for the presentation made and the information shared. With this, this meeting has concluded. Wassalaamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakaatuhu.
